artifacts.summary: Six-phase plan landing both ruled mechanisms (--task plus a canonical pre-commit Containment self-check) uniformly across fifteen implementation-agent definitions, with a live pre-fix regression case and the git-commit-scoped.sh chokepoint recorded as a follow-up.

memory_candidates.content: A guard mechanism that must fire mid-dispatch cannot be sited at a postflight or cycle-plan layer in this orchestration system, because the cycle-level artifacts those layers build (notably specs/.contention-manifest/*.json, built once per /orchestrate cycle by build_contended_manifest) are not rebuilt while an agent is running and may be overwritten by other cycles during a long dispatch. When planning a guard, first ask at what point in the dispatch lifecycle it must fire; that answer eliminates whole layers of candidate sites before any mechanism is weighed. Relatedly, a lease or contention mechanism keyed on declared-scope OVERLAP (two or more tasks declaring one path) is structurally blind to a path declared by NO task, so it can never substitute for a CONTAINMENT check (one concrete path tested against one declared scope). The two predicates are not interchangeable and a ruling that proposes one for the other's hazard is wrong on its face.
